notes: Read all 35 source lines line by line before editing. Imports: `useCallback` from react (L1) is preserved; `useLocation`/`useSearchParams` from react-router-dom (L2) are browser-only (no URL/router on native) so per contract rule 7 they are replaced by a native-safe in-process query store read via React's useSyncExternalStore — the same seam the sibling useAlertContext.ts port and the inlined EfficiencyPage.tsx URL store use.

JSDoc (L4-13): the SavedViewMenu-contract intent, the 'canonical querystring without leading ?' semantics, the `apply('')` clear-to-unfiltered behaviour, and the 'why a separate hook (avoid duplicating location.search.replace(/^?/,'') + setSearchParams boilerplate)' rationale are all carried over and expanded in the native header, plus an explicit native-divergence section naming the missing browser primitives and capturing nativeSavedViewUrlCapabilities.

Public surface (L14-17): the return type `{ currentQuery: string; apply: (query: string) => void }` is ported verbatim — exported `useSavedViewUrl()` returns the identical shape so the native consumers (EfficiencyPage SavedViewMenu via savedView.currentQuery/savedView.apply, and the web adopters EnergyPage/StatisticsPage/ChargingListPage/CostAnalysisPage/DrivesListPage/TripListPage/AlertsListPage/SignalsWorkspacePage/SignalDiffPage) keep the same contract.

`const location = useLocation()` (L18) and `const [, setSearchParams] = useSearchParams()` (L19) -> there is no react-router location/setSearchParams on native, so the URL is backed by a module-level store (currentQuerySnapshot + listeners). The hook subscribes via useSyncExternalStore(subscribeSavedViewQuery, getSavedViewQuery, getSavedViewQuery), the native equivalent of react-router re-rendering consumers when location.search changes.

currentQuery derivation (L21-23): web strips a leading '?' from location.search. Native stores the already-normalized querystring (no '?'), so currentQuery returns the store value directly; the leading-'?'-strip is still applied defensively inside replaceSavedViewQuery so parity holds regardless of input.

apply via useCallback (L25-32): preserved as `useCallback((query) => replaceSavedViewQuery(query), [])` with stable identity (mirrors web's useCallback(..., [setSearchParams]) where setSearchParams is stable, so callers can put apply in dep arrays). The web `setSearchParams(new URLSearchParams(query), { replace: false })` (L29) maps to replaceSavedViewQuery(query): it normalizes via `new URLSearchParams(query).toString()` (same serialized form react-router writes to location.search; empty string clears all params per the L27-28 comment) and notifies subscribers. The `{ replace: false }` history-push semantics have no native counterpart (no browser history stack) and are documented as a no-op in nativeSavedViewUrlCapabilities.

return { currentQuery, apply } (L34) and the closing brace (L35) ported verbatim. Explicit unavailable browser state (contract rule 7): browser URL + react-router location/searchParams -> in-process subscribable query store exposed via getSavedViewQuery/subscribeSavedViewQuery + a module-level replaceSavedViewQuery/clearSavedViewQuery bridge for the native navigation/deep-link layer to seed or restore a saved view from outside React; all captured in nativeSavedViewUrlCapabilities (browserUrlAvailable/reactRouterLocationAvailable false, inMemoryQueryStoreAvailable true, historyPushReplaceAvailable false).

No DOM modules, browser HTML elements, Recharts, Leaflet, localStorage, or old web UI components imported — only React (useCallback/useSyncExternalStore) and the global URLSearchParams (already used pervasively across the native parity api hooks). No i18n strings or unit conversions exist in this source, so none were introduced. EfficiencyPage.tsx keeps its own inlined URL store (which also backs useUrlString/useUrlBatch date-range mirroring) and was intentionally not modified to avoid splitting its shared from/to source-of-truth; this canonical hook is a faithful standalone port. Verified via npm run typecheck, npm run lint -- --quiet, and npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles.
